page: Microsoft Azure D64nls_v6 is an x86_64 virtual machine based on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, positioned in Azure's compute-dense general purpose segment. The server is powered by a dedicated 32-core Intel Xeon 8573C processor supporting two threads per core to deliver 64 vCPUs with clock frequencies up to 4.2 GHz. The CPU architecture includes a 260 MB Level 3 cache along with hardware execution extensions including Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) and AVX-512. The configuration is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, which establishes a 1:2 compute-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

Benchmark assessments demonstrate solid multi-threaded performance and high data throughput across diverse operational loads. In Geekbench testing, the machine ranks in the top ten percent for multi-core performance (21,489.0) and image processing, supported by strong results in Clang software compilation and ray tracing. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate high transfer rates, delivering 244.26 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 4,126.81 GB/sec on cached reads. In real-world application benchmarks, the instance recorded static web serving throughput of 89.28 GB/sec and 72.31 million Redis SET operations per second, along with strong prompt processing speeds on small and medium language models.

The D64nls_v6 is a diskless instance that provides no integrated local storage and no hardware GPU accelerators, necessitating remote Premium Storage attachments for operating system and data volumes. The reduced memory ratio delivers resource efficiency for CPU-bound tasks where large RAM capacities are not necessary. This hardware profile suits parallelized compute workloads, multi-threaded software compilation, CI/CD runners, network-heavy web proxies, and batch processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D64nls_v6 is an x86_64 virtual machine configured within Azure's general purpose and network-optimized families, emphasizing compute density over memory volume. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz, the instance supplies 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading and 260 MB of L3 cache. It is paired with 128 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The server lacks bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions, and contains no hardware accelerators or GPUs. In benchmarks, the D64nls_v6 exhibits strong multi-core processing performance, achieving high-throughput clang compilation, ray tracing, and static web serving reaching 89.28 GB/sec. It also demonstrates strong performance in Redis operations and CPU-based LLM prompt processing. This configuration fits compute-heavy tasks with modest memory footprints, such as continuous integration, web application serving, and multi-threaded data processing.
